## RCA — 2f46 rebar-gerrit autodeploy unhealthy (2026-08-29→30, us-east-1, acct 896586841071)

**Protocol:** `/rebar-debug` Phase 1 (Understand). Investigation was READ-ONLY against AWS/the Gerrit host (CloudWatch alarm-transition history + metrics; SSM `journalctl`/`docker`/`df` probes). No infra, config, or source change was made. Disposition = **STOP + ESCALATE** (every candidate fix is behavior/infra altering, not a bounded local-code defect fix). Ticket left `in_progress`, not closed.

### Verdict on the (a)/(b)/(c) question
**(a) — recurrence of an already-known, operator-ACCEPTED design limitation that has now become a problem in practice.** It is NOT a regressed fix, NOT downstream of disk bug e4f3 (b), and NOT genuinely new (c). The dedup `duplicates`→6af7 on this ticket is a **triage mis-dedup** (see below); the mechanism actually belongs to **40a7** (`surreal-horsy-skimmer`, closed `not_a_bug`).

### Proven mechanism #1 — `deploy_errors ×11` + `mcp-retire-cap ×11` (same event)
- SSM journal shows the 11 `mcp-retire-cap` and the bulk of `deploy_errors` are **time-locked to the same ticks**: `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP reason=port-exhausted "both 8092 and 8093 held by un-reaped mcp containers; cap=3"` alongside `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR reason=deploy_failed component=mcp target=… fail#N backoff`. Same timestamps ⇒ one event surfacing on two alarms.
- Root mechanism = **40a7**: `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:743` sets uvicorn `timeout_graceful_shutdown=int(grace_seconds)` with `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS=1200` (line 51). For a Streamable-HTTP MCP server, connected clients hold long-lived streams, so uvicorn graceful shutdown burns the **full 1200 s** even when the in-flight gauge is 0. `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` sets `MCP_STOP_GRACE=1260` (line 169) and only **two** rotation ports (`MCP_PORT_A/B=8092/8093`; 8091 reserved) with `MCP_RELEASES_CAP=3` (line 168). A retiring container pins one port for ~20 min; a second mcp deploy inside that window finds no free port → `port-exhausted` → `deploy_failed` + backoff, re-tried each ~120 s tick.
- Runtime confirmation: container `rebar-mcp-1f1606b93965-8092` first `docker stop --time 1260` at ts 1788029283, reaped at 1788030592 = **1309 s** later (full grace + SIGKILL), i.e. it did NOT fast-drain despite 0 in-flight. Coupling is **still live in current `origin/main`**.
- Cadence driver (what pushed an accepted ceiling over the edge): in-window there were **14 distinct mcp deploy targets** and **142 review-bot redeploys** (139 deferrals) — a high-cadence landing burst. 14 mcp rotations through a 2-port pool with ~20 min port-hold each is exactly the 40a7 congestion regime, at scale, for the first time.
- **40a7 was closed `not_a_bug` by explicit OPERATOR DECISION**: "mcp deploys capped ~1/20min whenever a client holds a session; **if that ceiling ever becomes a problem in practice, reopen this ticket.**" That condition is now met (11 alarm cycles in one burst).

### Proven mechanism #2 — `review-interrupts signal-unavailable ×2`
- Emitted by `autodeploy.sh:846` (`marker AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT signal-unavailable`) when `bot_in_flight_reviews()` (line 283) returns **-1** — curl to `http://localhost:8000/health` failed / `in_flight` unparseable — AND a review-bot deploy is triggered. The bot is then recreated **fail-open, without the drain check** (the marker exists precisely to make that blind deploy observable).
- Raw markers have distinct real timestamps ~daily ~16:50–17:05 PDT across 08-28/29/30 (1787961940, 1788047355/1788047692, 1788133956), and the metric datapoints are published at those real times — so these are **genuine fail-opens, NOT the e2a6 cold-start republish** (interrupt-signal offset file present = 5, not absent; e2a6 RULED OUT).
- On 08-29 the firing coincides with `bot-build-failed` (ts 1788047559): the review-bot was down/rebuilding (its own `compose build/up review-bot` takes `/health` down), and a subsequent tick read `in_flight=-1`. The daily regularity points at a periodic bot rebuild/unreachability window, driven by the same high redeploy cadence (142 bot redeploys in-window).

### Hypothesis (b) — disk bug e4f3 — REJECTED as the cause (decisive timing)
- e4f3's ticket comments were empty in-store, so I used CloudWatch `root-disk-pressure` alarm transitions directly. Windows (PDT):
  - `mcp-retire-cap`: ALL 11 between **08-29 14:50 → 08-30 03:06**.
  - `deploy_errors`: 10 of 11 on **08-29** (14:50→22:41); 1 on 08-30 16:58.
  - `root-disk-pressure` (e4f3): first sustained in-window flap **08-30 10:58**, then 11:53 / 12:27 / 15:43 / 16:47 — i.e. **entirely AFTER retire-cap had stopped (03:06)**.
- Effect cannot precede cause: disk pressure that begins 08-30 10:58 cannot have driven retire-cap/deploy_errors that ran 08-29 14:50→08-30 03:06. The dominant ×11/×11 pattern is 40a7 and PREDATES the disk flaps. ⇒ 2f46 is a **distinct concurrent issue, not downstream of e4f3** — do NOT defer/merge/double-fix.
- The **only** plausible disk contribution is the single 08-30 ~16:50 cluster (the lone 08-30 16:58 `deploy_errors` + the 08-30 16:53 `signal-unavailable`, both ~minutes after disk ALARM 16:47). Even those have an independent explanation (40a7 congestion; daily bot-rebuild unreachability). Note it as a secondary, partial overlap — not the cause.

### Also ruled out
- **6af7 recurrence:** 6af7 = `AuthConfigError`/secrets-not-refreshed (fixed via Gerrit 2230), a DIFFERENT `deploy_failed` cause. No `AuthConfigError`/secrets markers appear in-window. The `duplicates`→6af7 link is a mis-dedup; the correct mechanism ticket is 40a7.

### Attribution (origin of the mechanism)
- `git blame src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:743` → commit **8297083532a3f6f87754f34eb64f010e8d14e8f0** ("Add rebar-mcp HTTP service to the AWS box", 2026-08-24), which carries `rebar-ticket: fd4a-4e91-f179-4932` (story "rebar-mcp HTTP transport service on the AWS box"). This introduced `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS=1200` and the uvicorn-grace coupling.
- This matches 40a7's own attribution: 40a7 had a `caused_by`→fd4a edge and **removed it on its `not_a_bug` close, with a note to restore it if reopened**. I am deliberately NOT writing a `caused_by` edge here because the defect *legitimacy* is exactly what is being escalated (40a7 judged this intended behavior). Recommended: if the operator reopens 40a7 as a defect, restore `caused_by 40a7 → fd4a` (and/or `2f46 → fd4a`) at that point.

### Escalation (why this stops at Phase 1)
Every candidate fix is behavior/infra-altering — NOT a bounded, reversible, local-code defect fix — so per the skill this must be escalated, not auto-applied:
1. **Decouple** uvicorn `timeout_graceful_shutdown` from the certified-op grace (e.g. fast-drain to a short shutdown once the in-flight gauge hits 0, instead of always burning 1200 s). Blast radius: changes MCP shutdown semantics; risks cutting a genuinely-draining op short.
2. **Expand** the blue-green mcp port pool / raise `MCP_RELEASES_CAP`. Blast radius: infra/config (nginx upstreams, firewalling, reserved ports).
3. **Distinguish** "bot mid-redeploy" (expected transient `/health` outage) from "bot wedged" before fail-open recreation, so signal-unavailable stops firing on normal redeploys. Blast radius: changes the drain-gate decision logic.

**Recommended tracker actions (for operator):** reopen 40a7 (its reopen condition is now met); re-point 2f46's dedup from 6af7 to 40a7; treat e4f3 as a separate concurrent P2.

*Evidence base: CloudWatch alarm-transition histories + metric datapoints for all four alarms; read-only SSM `journalctl`/`docker`/`df` probes on i-00880b2c7f13527c5; git blame of `_mcp_health.py:743`. Investigation READ-ONLY throughout; no mutations applied.*

compiled_state.description:
## Surface
AWS CloudWatch, us-east-1, acct 896586841071, host `rebar-gerrit`. Three correlated autodeploy alarms flapped 2026-08-29→30: `deploy_errors` ×11, `mcp_retire_cap` ×11, `review_interrupts_signal_unavailable` ×2. Deploy path is fail-safe (no outage) but releases were not landing cleanly and in-flight reviews may have been killed blind. Full RCA + evidence is in this ticket's RCA comment.

## Root cause (proven — detail in the RCA comment)
**Mechanism 1 (deploy_errors ×11 + mcp-retire-cap ×11, one event).** `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py` sets uvicorn `timeout_graceful_shutdown=int(grace_seconds)` (line 743) with `grace_seconds` defaulting to the 1200s certified-op drain budget `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS` (line 51), and `make_sigterm_handler` sets `server.should_exit=True` **before** draining the in-flight gauge. Streamable-HTTP clients hold long-lived streams, so uvicorn's graceful shutdown waits the full 1200s for idle held-open streams even at 0 in-flight. With only two blue-green ports a retiring container pins a port ~20 min → the next mcp deploy hits `port-exhausted` → `deploy_failed` + backoff. A landing burst drove it 11×.

**Mechanism 3 (signal-unavailable ×2).** In `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` the drain gate reads the bot `/health` `in_flight`; on an unreadable signal `bot_in_flight_reviews()` returns `-1` and the gate **fails open** — recreates the bot with no drain check, emitting `AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT signal-unavailable`. It cannot tell a bot that is **mid-redeploy** (unreachable only because it is being recreated / still starting) from one genuinely **wedged**; the blind recreate can kill the very startup it should wait for.

## Approach
Two independent, bounded, reversible fixes; each with its own RED→GREEN test.

**Fix 1 — decouple uvicorn graceful-shutdown from the certified-op grace (`_mcp_health.py`).**
- Add a short constant `DEFAULT_UVICORN_GRACEFUL_SECONDS` for `uvicorn.Config(timeout_graceful_shutdown=...)`, decoupled from `grace_seconds` (which stays the op-drain budget); thread it as a defaulted `uvicorn_graceful_seconds` param on `run_http_with_grace` for testability.
- Reorder `make_sigterm_handler._on_sigterm` to drain the gauge FIRST (existing `drain_then_exit`, bounded by `grace_seconds`) and set `server.should_exit=True` only AFTER the gauge hits 0. A real in-flight op's streaming response then completes normally; once the gauge is 0, uvicorn's short backstop sweeps idle held-open streams in seconds instead of the full 1200s.
- Close NEW intake at SIGTERM so the fast-drain-at-0 cannot be re-pinned by a landing burst: add a `draining` flag to `InFlightGauge` (`begin_draining()`), and have the certified-op wrapper REFUSE a new certified op (raise `MCPRetiringError`, never incrementing) once draining. `_on_sigterm` calls `begin_draining()` FIRST (immediate intake-stop), before the drain loop; a certified request arriving mid-drain is rejected so the client retries the live (green) container and the gauge can actually reach 0. (uvicorn's `should_exit`-first intake-stop cannot be reused: with a short `timeout_graceful_shutdown` it would force-close a real in-flight op.) Ops already counted still drain to completion.
- Invariant preserved: >0 in-flight ⇒ full `grace_seconds` drain (never cut a real op short); 0 in-flight ⇒ fast drain; new intake refused during drain ⇒ a burst cannot extend the window or re-pin the port. The op bound is enforced by the gauge poll, never uvicorn's short backstop.

**Fix 3 — distinguish "bot mid-redeploy" from "bot wedged" (`autodeploy.sh`).**
- Add best-effort `bot_unreachable_disposition()` inspecting the bot container's docker state/health → `redeploying` (status `restarting`/`created`/`removing`/`paused`, or health `starting`) vs `wedged` (running-but-unreachable, `unhealthy`, no container, or any inspect error → default `wedged`).
- In the drain gate's `inflight < 0` branch, when `redeploying`, DEFER (retry next tick) with a countable `AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED bot-redeploying` marker, bounded by the existing `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX` episode; on bound-exhaustion or `wedged`, fall through to the existing fail-open recreate + `signal-unavailable`. Maps the single unknown `-1` onto its own disposition instead of a blind fail-open (mirrors the 1c0d disposition-contract intent).
- Invariant preserved: a wedged/down bot still fails open and deploys (recovery path); the mid-redeploy defer is bounded so it cannot live-lock the gate; any docker error defaults to `wedged` (pre-fix behavior).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py` — Fix 1 only. No change to `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS` (stays 1200), the gauge, or `drain_then_exit`.
- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` — Fix 3 only. No change to the `inflight > 0` busy-defer path, the port pool, or `MCP_RELEASES_CAP`.
- Tests otherwise. **Deferred / out of scope:** raising `MCP_RELEASES_CAP` / expanding the port pool (Option 2); any nginx/compose capacity change; the concurrent disk bug e4f3.

## Testing
- Fix 1 (`tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py`): the pre-existing `test_make_sigterm_handler_stops_intake_then_drains` (asserting the OLD `should_exit`-first ordering Fix 1 reverses) is REWRITTEN — not kept green — into `..._drains_gauge_before_stopping_intake_2f46`, asserting `should_exit` stays False while the gauge is >0 and flips only after it hits 0 (fast-drain + >0-in-flight guard); the `installs_sigterm_and_bounds` test's `timeout_graceful_shutdown` assertion is updated from `== 1200` to `== DEFAULT_UVICORN_GRACEFUL_SECONDS`. New tests: decoupled `timeout_graceful_shutdown` (< 1200s grace); and a new certified op during draining refused (`MCPRetiringError`) without incrementing the gauge. Other `run_http_with_grace` callers (startup-handshake / opcert / tool-offload) assert no such ordering and are unaffected.
- Fix 3 (`tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py`, real-bash stub harness): mid-redeploy bot (unreachable `/health` + docker `starting`/`restarting`) is DEFERRED (no `compose build/up`, `AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED bot-redeploying`, no `signal-unavailable`, deployed-sha unchanged, rc 0); wedged bot (unreachable + docker `running`) still fails open (`compose build` runs, `signal-unavailable` counted); the mid-redeploy defer is bounded (`DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX=0` falls through to fail-open).
- `make lint` + `make typecheck` + the two test modules; mutation check with teeth on the changed logic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A retiring MCP container with 0 in-flight certified ops shuts down within the short `DEFAULT_UVICORN_GRACEFUL_SECONDS` backstop (not the 1200s op grace), proven by a test asserting `timeout_graceful_shutdown == DEFAULT_UVICORN_GRACEFUL_SECONDS < DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS`.
- [ ] A retiring MCP container with >0 in-flight certified ops still receives the full `grace_seconds` drain and is never cut short, proven by a test asserting `should_exit` stays False until the gauge reaches 0.
- [ ] A NEW certified op arriving after SIGTERM (during the drain) is REFUSED (`MCPRetiringError`) and does not increment the gauge, while an already-in-flight op is unaffected — so a burst cannot re-pin the retiring port for the full grace. Proven by a gauge-level and a handler-level test.
- [ ] An unreadable `/health` caused by a mid-redeploy bot yields a DEFER with a countable `AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED bot-redeploying` marker and no `compose build/up`, asserted by the bash harness.
- [ ] A genuinely wedged/down bot (or an exhausted mid-redeploy defer bound) still fails open, runs `compose build`, and emits the countable `AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT signal-unavailable` marker, asserted by the bash harness.
- [ ] No capacity change is made: `MCP_RELEASES_CAP` and the blue-green port set are unchanged; both fixes are in-process/host-local with no CI-provider dependency.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the two targeted test modules pass; each mechanism has an independent RED→GREEN test.

file_impact.reason: Fix 1: decouple uvicorn timeout_graceful_shutdown from the 1200s certified-op grace (new DEFAULT_UVICORN_GRACEFUL_SECONDS constant + run_http_with_grace param/Config); reorder make_sigterm_handler to drain the in-flight gauge before setting should_exit so 0-in-flight drains fast and >0-in-flight keeps full grace.

Fix 3: add bot_unreachable_disposition() and branch the drain gate's inflight<0 case so a mid-redeploy bot is DEFERRED (bounded) with a countable AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED bot-redeploying marker instead of a blind fail-open; a wedged bot still fails open.
RED->GREEN tests for Fix 1: drain-before-stop ordering (fast-drain at 0 + >0-in-flight full-grace preservation) and uvicorn graceful-shutdown decoupled to the short constant.
RED->GREEN tests for Fix 3: mid-redeploy bot deferred (not recreated blind); wedged bot still fails open; mid-redeploy defer is bounded.
